improvementPriorities.title: Anchor answers in real project examples
improvementPriorities.whyItMatters: The role requires proven ability in Angular, C#, and scalable application design. Theoretical knowledge alone does not demonstrate this.
improvementPriorities.action: For every technical question, prepare to lead with a concise story: "In my project [X], I used [Angular/C#] to solve [Y] by doing [Z], which resulted in [outcome]."

improvementPriorities.title: Demonstrate code quality and scalability
improvementPriorities.whyItMatters: This is a direct requirement gap. Interviewers need to hear how you've written clean, maintainable code in a professional setting.
improvementPriorities.action: Prepare one detailed example of a feature or module you built with Angular and C#. Explain your design decisions, how you ensured maintainability, and any performance considerations.

improvementPriorities.title: Quantify your experience and impact
improvementPriorities.whyItMatters: The role seeks 5+ years of focused experience. Generic answers don't convey depth or the scale of projects you've handled.
improvementPriorities.action: For your key projects, be ready to state the project duration, your core contribution, the technologies used (Angular version, .NET version), and a tangible result or metric.

improvementPriorities.title: Address the CI/CD and DevOps gap
improvementPriorities.whyItMatters: This is listed as 'highly desirable.' Showing even foundational experience here would significantly strengthen your profile.
improvementPriorities.action: Reflect on any exposure to build pipelines, automated testing, or deployment processes. Frame it as a real example, not a hypothetical understanding.

coachingAdvice.advice: Immediately connect questions about skills or scenarios to a past project. This builds credibility from the first sentence.
coachingAdvice.example: Instead of "I know how to build scalable apps," say "On my last major Angular project, I designed the frontend architecture to handle scale by implementing lazy loading and a state management pattern, which reduced initial load time by 30%."

coachingAdvice.theme: Structure answers with context, action, result
coachingAdvice.advice: This simple framework forces you to provide the concrete details interviewers need to evaluate your experience.
coachingAdvice.example: Context: 'Our app had slow data retrieval.' Action: 'I used Entity Framework to optimize the queries, adding specific indexing and moving complex logic to stored procedures.' Result: 'This cut the average API response time from 2 seconds to 200ms.'

coachingAdvice.advice: Build 2-3 core stories that directly map to the job's focus areas: building Angular/.NET apps, optimizing data layers, and collaborating on delivery.
coachingAdvice.example: Have one story ready about a specific Angular feature you built, one about optimizing a SQL/Entity Framework data access layer, and one about collaborating with stakeholders to refine requirements.

coachingAdvice.advice: When you start to say "I would...", pause and ask yourself if you have a similar real experience. If you do, use that story instead.
coachingAdvice.example: Instead of "I would use AWS for deployment," say "In a previous project, I was involved in deploying our application to AWS, where I configured the S3 buckets for static assets and helped set up the EC2 instance parameters."

answerRewriteExamples.weak: I understand the importance of clean code and would make sure to write maintainable services in C#.
answerRewriteExamples.better: In my last project, I was responsible for the payment service in C#. I ensured maintainability by adhering to SOLID principles, writing unit tests with xUnit for all business logic, and using dependency injection, which made the code easy to modify and reduced bugs in subsequent releases.

answerRewriteExamples.weak: I can work with SQL and Entity Framework for data access.
answerRewriteExamples.better: For the reporting module on Project X, I used Entity Framework Core with SQL Server. I optimized a critical query that was timing out by rewriting it to use a compiled query and adding a covering index, which improved the load time for the report from 15 seconds to under 2 seconds.

answerRewriteExamples.weak: If I was building a scalable web app, I would use Angular for the frontend and .NET for the backend.
answerRewriteExamples.better: I recently built a customer portal using Angular 15 and .NET 6. To ensure scalability, I implemented micro-frontend architecture for independent team deployment, used server-side pagination for large data sets, and designed the .NET Web API with asynchronous processing, supporting a 50% increase in user load without performance degradation.
